context: Follow-ups after the Rails 5.2 -> 8.1.4 / Ruby 4.0.7 port (branch major-up, uncommitted).

items.title: Keep orchestration state out of git before committing the port
items.description: The Rails 8 port is uncommitted on branch major-up. The `.omo/` directory (plans, evidence, notepads) is untracked and would be swept in by `git add -A`. Decide whether to keep the local rollback tag `pre-rails8-port`.
acceptance: .omo/ is ignored (.gitignore or .git/info/exclude) and `git status --porcelain` shows no `?? .omo/`
Port changes committed in reviewable commits on major-up
Tag pre-rails8-port deleted or intentionally kept
items.notes: Rollback anchor until committed: git reset --hard pre-rails8-port && git clean -fd

items.title: Resolve Kamal deploy config that references a missing Dockerfile
items.description: The Rails 8 skeleton brought config/deploy.yml, bin/kamal and the kamal gem, but the Dockerfile was intentionally not copied, so a Kamal deploy would fail.
acceptance: Either config/deploy.yml, bin/kamal and the kamal gem are removed and `bundle install` still succeeds, OR a Dockerfile is added and `docker build .` succeeds
items.notes: thruster and bin/docker-entrypoint are part of the same decision.

items.title: Verify production mode (Solid Cable/Queue/Cache, asset precompile)
items.description: All verification ran in development, where Action Cable uses the async adapter. Production uses solid_cable plus separate SQLite databases for cache/queue/cable, which were never exercised.
acceptance: `RAILS_ENV=production bin/rails db:prepare` creates primary, cache, queue and cable databases
`RAILS_ENV=production bin/rails assets:precompile` succeeds and includes the dartsass-built application.css
A production-mode server serves / with 200 and delivers an Action Cable message between two browsers via solid_cable

items.title: Make the test suite run
items.description: test/ mixes Rails 5 generated stubs/fixtures with the Rails 8 skeleton test_helper and has never been run after the port.
acceptance: `bin/rails test` exits 0
Obsolete generated stubs/fixtures removed or fixed
At least one integration test covers login, posting a message and admin delete
items.notes: Useful before the security fixes so behaviour can be pinned first.

items.title: Fix local Ruby toolchain ergonomics
items.description: The gem executable dir /usr/local/lib/ruby/gems/4.0.0/bin is not on PATH (so `rails` resolves to the macOS /usr/bin/rails stub), and every `gem` command prints "already initialized constant RDoc::..." warnings because rdoc 8.0.0 lives in ~/.local/share/gem/ruby/4.0.0 while the system rdoc plugin points at rdoc 7.0.4.
acceptance: `which rails` resolves to the gem bin dir in a new shell
`gem env` prints no RDoc constant warnings
items.notes: Machine-level change outside the repo (shell rc / gem dirs).

items.title: Stop message impersonation and unauthenticated posting
items.description: MessagesController#create trusts `message[user_id]` from a hidden form field, has no login check and no group-membership check, so anyone can post as any user into any group.
acceptance: Logged-out POST /messages/create redirects to /login and creates no Message
A tampered message[user_id] is ignored; the message is attributed to current_user
Posting to a group the user is not a member of is rejected
The hidden user_id field is removed from the form
items.notes: Build via current_user.messages.build(content:, group:) and permit only :group_id, :content.

items.title: Restrict group edit/update to the group owner
items.description: GroupsController#edit and #update have no ownership check, so any visitor can rename a group or change its members.
acceptance: GET /groups/:id/edit and PATCH /groups/:id by a non-owner redirect without changes
Logged-out requests redirect to /login
The owner can still edit

items.title: Scope Action Cable broadcasts per group
items.description: MessagesChannel streams from one global 'messages' stream, so every browser receives every group's messages; privacy is only client-side filtering. Identify the connection by the session user and stream per group.
acceptance: Connection uses identified_by :current_user from the session and rejects anonymous connections
The channel subscribes per group and rejects non-members
A member of group Y receives no WebSocket frame for a message posted to group X
The README 'Known limitations' entries for the global stream and anonymous connections are removed
items.notes: Removes the need for the client-side groupName/42 sentinel filter.

items.title: Logged-out GET /groups/:id raises a 500
items.description: has_access_to_group? calls current_user.groups while current_user is nil.
acceptance: Logged-out GET /groups/1 redirects to /login (302), no 500

items.title: Channel JS throws TypeError on pages without #groupname
items.description: renderMessage reads document.querySelector('#groupname').innerText with no null check, so a broadcast arriving on any non-group page throws.
acceptance: With a browser on / and another user posting a message, the first browser's console shows no errors
items.notes: Largely obsoleted by SEC-3, but cheap to guard.

items.title: Message textarea allows 300 chars but the model allows 200
items.description: Messages of 201-300 characters fail validation with only the generic mess_error flash.
acceptance: The textarea maxlength matches the model's maximum length (200)

items.title: Failed-login error rendered twice and mentions email
items.description: sessions/new renders flash.now[:danger] and the layout also renders flash[:danger]; the text says 'Invalid email/password combination' although login uses a nickname.
acceptance: A failed login shows the error exactly once
The message reads 'Invalid nickname/password combination'
items.notes: Verify the duplication in a browser first.

items.title: 'User deleted' flash is never displayed
items.description: UsersController#destroy sets flash[:success] but neither the layout nor users/index renders it (pre-existing, confirmed identical before the port).
acceptance: After an admin deletes a user, /users shows 'User deleted' once
items.notes: Consider one flash partial in the layout for all keys (success, warning, danger, mess_error), replacing per-view flash blocks.

items.title: Remove hardcoded group id 1 / user id 1
items.description: users#create auto-joins group_id 1, users/show links '/groups/1', and seeds hardcode owner_id/user_id 1, so everything breaks on a non-virgin database.
acceptance: The community group is looked up by name (or a flag), not by id
`bin/rails db:seed` is idempotent and uses associations, not literal ids
The README 'Known limitations' entry for hardcoded seed ids is removed

items.title: Remove unused image_processing gem
items.description: Skeleton default; the app does not use Active Storage.
acceptance: image_processing removed, `bundle install` and `bin/rails zeitwerk:check` pass

items.title: Remove the demo Stimulus hello_controller
items.description: The generator's example controller is unused.
acceptance: The file is deleted and `bin/importmap json` no longer lists controllers/hello_controller

items.title: Trim routes to the actions that exist
items.description: `resources :members` points at an empty controller and `resources :groups`/`:users` generate routes with no actions (e.g. GET /groups returns 404 ActionNotFound).
acceptance: Resources use only: [...] matching the implemented actions
`bin/rails routes` lists no route whose action is missing
The empty MembersController is removed if unused

items.title: Collapsible mobile navigation
items.description: Below 768px the header nav stacks vertically (faithful to the old Bootstrap 3 behaviour); a Bootstrap 5 navbar-toggler/collapse would fix it.
acceptance: At 375px width the header shows a toggler and the links open in a collapse
Desktop layout is unchanged
items.notes: Also consider data-bs-theme="dark" instead of the deprecated navbar-dark.

items.title: Consider Rails 8 built-in authentication
items.description: Optionally replace the hand-rolled session helpers with `bin/rails generate authentication`.
acceptance: Login/logout/signup behaviour is preserved and covered by tests
items.notes: Optional and larger in scope; requires a data migration for existing users.
